The estimated increase in database growth is 10GB per annum with accompanying image storage growth of approximately 2TB per annum. The Treatment Planning System is intended to be the departmentâs primary pre-treatment planning system for almost all radical and palliative treatments.

description:

Products may include, but are not limited to, pregnancy tests, HIV tests, syphilis tests and combination sexual health testing products. The Framework is intended to support the delivery of sexual health services by providing access to clinically appropriate, compliant and value for money diagnostic products across participating authorities. Lot 3 is a multi supplier unranked award, it evaluated and awarded independently of all other Lots.
 Tenderers may bid for this Lot without submitting a tender for any other Lot. Services may include, but are not limited to, products, educational resources, awareness campaigns, training materials, patient information, health promotion initiatives and other value-added activities designed to improve sexual health outcomes and support service delivery.

title: Occupational Health, Employee Assistance Programme and Associated Services
description: Work-focused medical assessments, advice on fitness for work, adjustments, health surveillance, and case-specific clinical guidance for SDS management. Note: OH will focus strictly on medical and capability advice in a workplace context or mandated work-related intervention (e.g. drug & alcohol counselling) and not be expected to provide general counselling or non-medical interventions, unless the provider is successful in multiple lots. 24/7 confidential counselling and advice for employees (and immediate family members as industry-standard, typically age 16+ dependents). Includes short-term counselling (phone/online/in-person) and practical advice (legal, financial, family, etc.), plus structured clinical triage to identify cases requiring other interventions (e.g. specialist therapy or OH referral). Communications & Engagement Support - proactive collaboration with SDSâs internal Communications to drive awareness and appropriate usage of the service (e.g. campaigns, uptake analysis, content for staff communications). e.g. Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), trauma-focused counselling, or other structured interventions beyond short-term EAP counselling. These are delivered via call-off following EAP or management recommendation (not automatically bundled into the core EAP fee). A non-clinical advice and coaching helpline for SDS managers dealing with difficult people situations (e.g. supporting staff with mental health issues, sensitive conversations, crisis support). Distinct from EAP, this service is intended to provide managers with practical guidance, coaching and emotional support when dealing with challenging workplace situations involving the wellbeing of employees. It is not a source of HR, legal or procedural advice and must not direct managers on employment decisions or formal people management processes. Responsibility for policy interpretation, case management and employment decisions remains with SDS. Specialist evaluations of employees potentially neurodivergent, with workplace-focused recommendations, delivered by qualified practitioners, separate from OH. Post-assessment support for individuals or teams to implement adjustments and build capability. Supply of recommended adjustments (chairs, desks, peripherals, etc.) via pre-defined catalogues/pricing. Provision of specialised software for disabled/neurodivergent employees and training to ensure effective use.
